title: Flow
description: What a person is walked through to define one kind of manifest: the steps, in order, and the fields each step asks for. Every interface renders a flow from this description, so a web screen and a terminal screen ask the same questions in the same order with the same words. A field is addressed by its path in the manifest (a JSON pointer), which is also how a check names the field it is about and how the conformance driver finds it.

id.description: The flow's id; one flow per manifest kind, named after it in lower case.

name.description: The standard noun for what is being defined, in the organisation's words via Settings when they differ.

for.description: The manifest kind this flow defines.

stages.description: The steps grouped into stages, the walk a person sees: each stage names its steps, and read in order the stages give every step once, in the order of steps. A stage gathers steps that decide one thing (who governs, what is produced), and comes after every stage whose answers it needs. Optional: a flow without stages is walked step by step.

guide.description: What the stage settles, in a sentence.

steps.description: The keys of its steps, in order.

prepare.description: What the walk picks from, to prepare before it starts, in the order of work (TAXONOMY.md D34): each kind its fields reference, after every kind it needs itself. A person adds what is missing here, one short step at a time, so the walk only picks. needed marks what a hand-over will want; the rest enriches. Nothing here is required to begin.

level.description: For Goal, the level the walk picks.

needed.description: Whether a hand-over of the work will need one.

guide.description: Why the walk wants it, in a sentence.

review.description: Whether the flow ends with a review step showing everything gathered before a version is saved.

key.description: Stable identifier; what a check's fix link and a driver's Step() name.

title.description: The standard term for the step (Aim, Measures, Scope), never a chatty paraphrase.

guide.description: One spoken sentence saying what the step settles, plain idea first.

links.description: Other manifests this step settles a link with, where the link is held on their side: a gap names the outcomes that would close it, so an outcome's step asks which gap it closes. Each is established before or with this manifest, reusing an existing one first.

phase.description: When in the work this is settled. Define says what each thing is (a gap's two states, an outcome's statement); measure gives it numbers (baselines and targets, from the sources at hand); align links it to the rest (which outcome a gap closes, which aims a KPI measures). Everything in define comes before measure, and measure before align, across every record of a project, programme or operation, so a person and an agent settle a strategy in the same order. A step without one defines; a field or link may differ from its step.

path.description: JSON pointer into the manifest; the schema at that path says the type, the enum, the reference target and the title.

control.description: How the field is asked for. choice: pick one of the schema's enum; reference: pick an existing manifest of the x-cartograph-ref kind, with a way to add one; references: pick several; list: a keyed list of items, each defined by the fields below; horizon: years and optional months with a 'same as above' choice.

title.description: Overrides the schema's title for this step only; otherwise the schema's title is the label.

hint.description: One spoken sentence shown while the field is empty. Never a placeholder inside the control.

key.description: For a list: the item property that identifies an item (the schema's x-cartograph-list-key). Items are merged by this key across editors.

fields.description: For a list: the fields of one item, paths relative to the item.

checks.description: Keys of the checks this field answers (SMART marks, completeness lines); shown beside the field as marks, never as prose.

kind.description: The kind that holds the link.

path.description: Where on that kind the link is held, as a JSON pointer; it names this manifest's id.

check.description: The check that reports whether the link is made.

needs.description: Which side is unfinished without the link, so a guide can lay out the work in order: holder when the kind holding it should name one (a gap should name the indicator that measures it), named when the manifest it names should be named by one (an outcome should be closed by a gap). Absent when neither is: a project citing a gap is work on it, not part of defining it.

level.description: For a Goal holding the link, the level it is at (a goal's objectives are objectives).

when.description: Applies only when the field at path holds one of the values in: an outcome's links, not a goal's.
